bullets.text: CR 89.3 with solid profitability across all lines except Property, where catastrophes added 30.6 points to CR; Commercial Lines delivered an 83.9 CR alongside strong Personal Lines margins.
Companywide NPW +19% YOY; Commercial Lines NPW surged 57%, driven by pandemic recovery, peak season, and stimulus dollars; March 17 was Progressive's second-highest Direct auto sales day ever.

Total PIF +12% YOY, passing 25M milestone; personal auto surpassed 17M and special lines 5M; double-digit growth across all segments for first time since 2004; Robinson PIFs up ~20% Direct, >16% Agency.

Progress on D&I objectives: if hiring volume holds, expects population parity for people of color in next few years and leadership gender parity by 2025; creating programs aimed at 'fixing the broken first rung.'
Personal Lines loss frequency rose YOY amid higher VMTs, seasonal weather losses, and special lines volume; VMT was down 8–10% versus prior years by late March; claims is staffing up.

Announced intent to acquire Protective Insurance for ~$338M ($23.30/share) to expand fleet and workers compensation capabilities; BOP expanded to 19 states (37% of CMP market); Snapshot Apron Relief offered in 43 states.

Personal auto model 8.6 in 32 states (59% countrywide premium, 67% PIFs) showed improved conversion; model 8.7 launched in January; 12 states are now operating on the new commercial policy administration system.

Investment portfolio returned 0.3% as equity market strength countered rising interest rates; portfolio duration slightly increased from year-end; management believes capital position remains strong against potential post-pandemic market volatility.

Launched new customer self-service website experience for all eligible policyholders following successful testing that demonstrated higher customer satisfaction and better self-service resolution for private passenger auto.

Starting in March 2021, YOY growth comparisons will be inflated due to prior-year depressed shopping and negative Commercial Lines growth; stimulus payments aided Q1 growth, driving near-record Direct auto sales on March 17.
